spec_match.rationale: Implements the explainer's headline use case with real injected <link rel=preload as=fetch> elements, reads preloads[].used as timestamp-or-null from the real getSpeculations(), and teaches the crucial nuance that null means not-consumed-yet and pagehide may be BFCache entry rather than waste.

interactive.rationale: Three real preload rows with per-row fetch-to-consume buttons, a read button, a reset, and a report pane whose data source (live API vs page bookkeeping) is explicitly disclosed.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises injecting real preloads, consuming some, reading the used field, and the null-vs-waste/BFCache caveat; the page delivers each element verbatim.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles method-absent with a clearly-labelled own-bookkeeping fallback that is never presented as the browser's verdict, fetch failures, a throwing read, and the BFCache caveat in both prose and code comments.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5118840377835520 plus the three sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The suite's preload-used-field-shape assertion encodes this page's contract; its failure in this Chromium 141 session is only the expected absent experimental method.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop screenshot shows the three idle rows with consume buttons and the injected preload links in head; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; consume/read/reset clicks could not be driven non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts consumption events, fetch failures, live reads with counts, and fallback reads with the consumed tally.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours and correct button overrides, but the consumed state renders --accent-emerald text on --bg-ivory at 0.72rem bold (~4.0:1), just under WCAG AA 4.5:1 — and it is a common-path state reachable in any browser.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled table, per-row buttons carry aria-labels naming the resource, disabled state on consumed rows, aria-live report pane, and status conveyed as text (idle/consumed) alongside colour.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (URLs word-break inside the table); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Raise the consumed-state text to AA contrast
openQuestions.detail: status-used renders --accent-emerald #0a8f5c on the ivory table row at 0.72rem bold, computing ~4.0:1 against the 4.5:1 AA bar — and unlike the flag-gated states this one appears the moment any visitor consumes a preload. A darker emerald token or pairing the colour with a bolder background chip would clear it; the same emerald-on-light pattern recurs across the corpus and deserves a design-system-level fix.

openQuestions.title: Verify the live used-timestamp flow in a SpeculationMeasurement-enabled build
openQuestions.detail: In this Chromium 141 only the labelled own-bookkeeping fallback is reachable. In a flagged build, consume one preload and leave two idle, then confirm the live report shows a numeric used timestamp for the consumed row and null for the others, matching the immutable preload-used-field-shape conformance assertion.

summary: The feature's headline use case built honestly: real preload links, real consumption fetches, and a report whose provenance (browser measurement vs page bookkeeping) is never blurred, with the BFCache caveat correctly taught. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): clean render and console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either class. Open items: the marginal consumed-state contrast and a flagged-build live verification.
